items.q: The definition of a podocytopathy on this page places the primary injury on the podocyte.
opts: True — the podocyte is named as the primary target, not the mesangium or the endothelium
False — podocytopathies are defined by primary mesangial cell injury
False — the term is reserved for diseases of the glomerular basement membrane
True — and every disease in the group carries the same risk of chronic kidney disease
items.exp: Glomerular diseases that primarily affect podocytes. (Book p762)

items.q: The clinical presentation list of glomerular diseases repeated here runs from asymptomatic and macroscopic hematuria through nephrotic/nephritic syndromes to RPGN and:
items.exp: Presentation list ends with chronic glomerulonephritis. (Book p762)

items.q: Match each podocytopathy with its CKD-risk label — 1) Minimal change disease 2) FSGS 3) Membranous nephropathy … A) >2/3rd → CKD even with Rx B) No risk for CKD C) 1/3rd → CKD if not treated
items.exp: Without podocytopenia: MCD (no CKD risk); with podocytopenia: FSGS >2/3rd → CKD even with Rx; MN 1/3rd → CKD if not treated. (Book p762)

items.q: The with-podocytopenia branch (the CKD-risk branch) names FSGS, membranous nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy; the entity NOT placed on that branch is:
items.exp: With podocytopenia: FSGS, MN, diabetic nephropathy (DN). (Book p762)

items.q: Match each 2° MCD item with its book annotation — 1) NSAIDs 2) Gold 3) Highlighted malignancy … A) Hodgkin's disease B) MN > MCD C) MCD > MN
items.exp: NSAIDs (MCD > MN); gold (MN > MCD); malignancy highlight: Hodgkin's disease. (Book p762)

items.q: The allergy branch of 2° MCD causes lists atopic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, asthma and:
items.exp: Allergy: atopic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, asthma, post-immunization. (Book p762)

items.q: Sezary syndrome, bracketed inside the malignancy line for minimal change disease, is described as a cutaneous T cell lymphoma.
opts: True — the bracket reads cutaneous T cell lymphoma
False — Sezary syndrome is the B-cell leukemia of that line
False — the bracket identifies it as a plasma cell dyscrasia
True — and Hodgkin's disease carries the same bracket
items.exp: Malignancy: Hodgkin's disease; Sezary syndrome (cutaneous T cell lymphoma); CLL. (Book p762)

items.q: The 100/0 rule of MCD presentation states that every patient of MCD presents with:
items.exp: 100/0 rule: every patient of MCD → nephrotic syndrome. (Book p762)

items.q: Hypertension, AKI and microhematuria are written as absent in MCD; the feature that IS expected is:
items.exp: Hypertension, AKI & microhematuria absent; nephrotic syndrome present (100/0 rule). (Book p762)

items.q: Which MCD presentation statement is TRUE?
opts: Every MCD patient presents with nephrotic syndrome, with hypertension, AKI and microhematuria absent
A quarter of MCD patients present with isolated hematuria
MCD commonly presents with hypertensive crisis
AKI is a routine presenting feature of MCD
items.exp: 100/0 rule; hypertension, AKI & microhematuria absent. (Book p762)

items.q: Fill up: The MCD rule that every patient presents with nephrotic syndrome is the ______ rule.
items.exp: 100/0 rule: every patient of MCD → nephrotic syndrome. (Book p762)
